facts: I led the discussion of the paradoxical behavior of mesons on the third and last day.
I kept interrupting with leading questions and summarizing where we were, pushing the others to think of solutions.
As I pulled the discussion together, Marshak, sitting next to Pais, suddenly went red in the face.
Marshak stood up and said: "Maybe there are two kinds of mesons. One kind is copiously produced, then disintegrates into a different kind which absorbs only weakly."
Weisskopf and several other physicists returning to Cambridge took me up on the invitation and flew with me.
Halfway there we ran into a storm.
The pilot decided to put down at a Navy base in New London, Connecticut, an airfield where civilian aircraft were forbidden.
As we taxied up to the dock, the pilot could see an angry Navy captain yelling at him. I told the pilot, "Let me handle this."
I stepped off the plane and announced, "My name is Oppenheimer."
The officer gasped and asked, "Are you the Oppenheimer?" I said, "I am an Oppenheimer."
He couldn't do enough for us after that: tea and cookies for me and my friends, and then a Navy bus to take us on to Boston.
